note: Suites we run that EvalScope also implements. EvalScope names ModelScope mirrors as its dataset ids, but its adapters read the ORIGINAL Hugging Face column names, so a mirror is a straight copy and we can point each benchmark at our own pinned snapshot instead. That is what makes this a cross-check rather than a second measurement: both harnesses read byte-identical data at the same commit, so any disagreement is scoring, not data. We do not pull from ModelScope.

suites.note: EvalScope's dataset id is TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro already; same repo, same pin as ours.

Same repo and pin as ours. EvalScope grades HLE with a judge and we grade string-match-then-judge, so compare the delta and never the absolute. EvalScope grades HLE with an LLM judge whose default is Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B at https://api-inference.modelscope.cn/v1/, so a run with a ModelScope token configured would send our outputs to a third party and put an unpinned remote judge in the gate. The bridge refuses unless a judge is named explicitly.
EvalScope names AI-ModelScope/gpqa_diamond but its adapter reads 'Question', 'Correct Answer' and 'Incorrect Answer 1..3', which are Idavidrein's own column names. Pointed at our pin instead.
suites.args_note: reformat_subset=False, so the subset is passed as the HF config name. EvalScope declares 'default', which is not a config of Idavidrein/gpqa, so the load fails without this.

suites.note: EvalScope evaluates the validation split; our suite scores 200 items of it.

Adapter reads id/question/options/answer/subject/topic_difficulty/image, which is MMMU_Pro's own schema. Its 'image' is the vision subset's single image where our adapter reads image_1..7 of the standard subset, so confirm which subset is loaded before trusting a comparison.
suites.args_note: Defaults to the 4-option set and warns; our suite scores the 10-option standard split.

suites.note: EvalScope executes generated code in the local environment and has no generate-only mode, so a cluster run would execute model-written code beside the checkpoints. The plugin adds an `execute` param: the cluster pass returns a deferred marker and never reaches the executor, then the isolated pass runs --use-cache --rerun-review with execute=True. Both must register as `live_code_bench`, since the prediction cache path is keyed by benchmark name, so the plugin swaps the adapter on the existing metadata rather than adding a second entry.
suites.args_note: execute=False for the generating pass; the scoring pass overrides it to True. The bridge marks deferred reviews and the comparator refuses any file containing one.

suites.note: EvalScope reads one record carrying prompt and key together, with functions/tools/turns/ground_truth as JSON strings; upstream ships prompts and possible_answer as two files. `bfcl-dataset` reshapes our pin into that layout, 3486 rows matching our own adapter exactly. Scoring then runs through Gorilla's official bfcl-eval, which is more authoritative than our AST reimplementation.
suites.args_note: multi_turn is excluded: those rows need an initial_config and the Gorilla simulators' state, which the static files do not carry.
